card.band: 4h. The lever is partly known (buffer fill and SIMD-friendly refill), but frontier agents vary on the range-sampling and Bool paths. Several independent hot paths give a steady curve. A weaker model breaks stream identity.
card.cheat: Switching to a different generator breaks stream identity. Caching outputs fails across seeds and sizes.
card.grading: Hard gate: bitwise-identical output streams for many seeds, types, sizes and ranges against recorded reference streams. The score is the median wall-clock speedup over a hidden benchmark set, reward 2^u-1 against our reference speedup.
card.reference: The merged upstream PR plus later follow-ups, with the speedup measured on the grader machine. The size is not found and must be measured.
card.task: /app ships a Julia stdlib Random snapshot at the pre-PR state, with a toolchain. The agent speeds up rand for MersenneTwister over integer types, arrays, ranges and bools without changing any output stream.
card.title: Julia MersenneTwister bulk rand speedup under a stream-identity gate

facts.claim: JuliaLang/julia PR #37914 'quite faster rand(::MersenneTwister, ::Type{Int})' exists and was merged on 2020-10-17 as commit b8bc81677ea4075d161a464dbb33f0eef33aa291
The seed's pin 'PR 37914 @ v1.13.2 line' cannot be the pre-PR base: the PR is already merged into the v1.13.2 line, so the snapshot must be taken from a commit before b8bc816 (about Oct 2020)
PR #37916 (rand Float64, Int32 etc. for MersenneTwister) was merged on 2020-10-07, ten days before #37914, so a pre-#37914 snapshot already contains its Float64 and small-integer speedups

The PR description reports about 1.8x for Int64/UInt64 scalar generation, about 1.6x for Int128/UInt128, and about 1.5x for ranges under 64 bits; the author says these are measured on their machine only (self-reported)
Julia v1.13.2 stdlib/Random/src contains MersenneTwister.jl, DSFMT.jl, generation.jl, normal.jl, Xoshiro.jl and related files
Repository licence is MIT (GitHub API spdx field; LICENSE file itself not opened)
Diff size of PR #37914 (added/removed lines) is shown on the PR page
Later follow-up PRs #58089 and #58306 tuned rand(1:n) performance
Reference speedup on the grader machine

spike_plan.kill_if: Reference speedup on the median benchmark is under 1.2x, run-to-run noise is over 15%, or the Julia build cannot be made offline
spike_plan.pass_if: Reference build is at least 1.5x faster on the Int and range buckets, streams are bit-identical across runs, and noise is under 10%
steps: In a networked container, clone JuliaLang/julia and check out the parent of b8bc816 (pre-#37914), then build with make -j8 and record the build time and downloaded deps
Check out b8bc816 as the reference build and build it the same way
Write a timing harness for rand(MT, Int64/Int128/UInt32), rand(1:n) for n<64 bits, rand(Bool), Float64 arrays and Bool arrays; run each build 5 times and take medians
Dump streams for many seeds, types, sizes and ranges from the pre-PR build; confirm the reference build reproduces them exactly and run the dump twice to confirm determinism
Compute reference speedup S per bucket and the noise (run-to-run spread) of the medians
Check whether the Julia build can be made fully offline by vendoring its download cache, and note the size

v1.summary: The seed is real and well-sourced: PR #37914 is merged (b8bc816, 2020-10-17), MIT-licensed, and its self-reported 1.5-1.8x speedups are public, but the seed's "@ v1.13.2" pin is wrong because the PR is already in that release, so the snapshot must be pre-b8bc816 and must already include #37916. Band is capped at 3 with E0 evidence, the build cost is unprobed (smoke_build {}), and the approach is partly recallable from upstream, so the seed should pass with conditions: a history-less pre-PR snapshot, a measured reference speedup, and a spike to confirm the build and speedup before committing.

v2.note: The base pin was contradicted: the snapshot would have to be a 2020 Julia tree (parent of b8bc816), and building it offline is costly and unprobed. The lever is one known, recallable trick (bulk dSFMT fill) and the PR diff is small. The speedup is self-reported (1.5-1.8x) and unmeasured, and gVisor wall-clock noise threatens the median. With 3.5 frontier hours in a 4h tier, there is not enough sustained work.
